purpose: T0.3 proper fix: parameterise the subgrid auto-adjust floor and find its optimum
build: c73ee4b6c213 (SubgridSizeAutoAdjustMinimum, default 2000 = bit-identical to prior behaviour)

config.note: 4 arms run concurrently on separate nodes; the winning arm repeated for timing confidence.

headline: floor=512 is 25.8% faster than the historical default (1685.7 s two-sample mean vs 2272.5 s), barrier -43% (798.6 vs 1408.8 s). Repeat spread 1.8%, i.e. within node scatter.

optimum_is_real_not_noise.observation: floor=256 balances BETTER (barrier 762 s, chem skew 1.87) yet runs SLOWER than 512.
optimum_is_real_not_noise.mechanism: Per-grid overhead overtakes the balance gain. Measured section totals as the floor drops 2000 -> 512 -> 256: SetBoundaryConditions 107 -> 133 -> 153 s, PrepareDensityField 82 -> 119 -> 143 s, CommReceiveHandler 102 -> 152 -> 182 s, SolveHydroEquations 110 -> 124 -> 131 s. Going 512 -> 256 buys only 27 s of barrier for ~81 s of extra overhead. This is the classic AMR granularity trade-off, measured end to end.

correctness.method: CORRECTED comparator (commit 92e436d0): hierarchy-derived cell volumes, child-masked baryon sums, particle dx^3.
correctness.reading: Conserved quantities conserved - dark matter at machine precision, baryon at 4.5e-10. Star formation differs 0.075% from the altered refinement: a real but small C2 difference, consistent with gas not converted to stars remaining baryonic.

why_this_beats_pinning_MaximumSubgridSiz: The adaptive formula keeps large grids where granularity is already fine (L4-L7 stay ~1000-2000 cells, 5-7 grids/rank) and shrinks only the starved deep levels. The earlier flat cap of 400 (t03-subgrid-r1) shrank every level indiscriminately and gained less (24% vs 25.8%) while paying ghost-zone overhead it did not need to.
recommendation: Adopt SubgridSizeAutoAdjustMinimum = 512 for FOGGIE production at 128 ranks. The parameter defaults to 2000 so no other Enzo user is affected. NOTE the optimum is scale-dependent: it is where the formula's per-level answer (364-413 cells here) meets rising per-grid overhead, so it should be re-measured if the rank count or refinement depth changes materially.
remaining_headroom: Berger-Rigoutsos still cannot split solidly-flagged regions, so the deep-level grid counts remain below what the cap requests. Audit T2.10 (forced/geometric bisection when a grid exceeds the cap) is the next lever.
